title: Longest Common Suffix Queries
summary: Given two arrays of strings, for each string in the query array, find the string in the container array that shares the longest common suffix.
statement: Given two arrays of strings, for each string in the query array, find the string in the container array that shares the longest common suffix. If multiple strings share the longest suffix and have the same minimum length, choose the one that appears first in the container array. Return an array of indices corresponding to the matched strings.
constraints: Both arrays contain nonempty lowercase strings.
For each query, maximize common suffix length with a container word, then prefer shorter container length and finally smaller index.
Return the selected container index for every query; a zero-length suffix still uses the length/index tie-breaks.
hints: Reversing every string turns common suffixes into ordinary trie prefixes.
At each trie node store the best container by (length,index); answer a query at its deepest reachable reversed prefix.
Insert reversed words while minimizing metadata at every node, then walk each reversed query until the first missing edge.
Trie depth is the common suffix length, and node metadata applies the two remaining tie-breaks among every word sharing that suffix.
editorial: Trie depth is the common suffix length, and node metadata applies the two remaining tie-breaks among every word sharing that suffix.

tests.explanation: Cd chooses index one by shortest length; bcd exactly matches index one; xyz has no suffix match and also chooses the shortest word at index one.
Za shares suffix a with all entries and chooses the shortest word at index zero; x shares nothing and also chooses index zero.
